review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form; a substantially shorter and refocused new submission could be worth evaluating, but the cumulative manuscript should not receive another ordinary revision round.
blocking_findings: The executed evidence does not establish an incremental numerical contribution from the learned Bellman critic.
The costate-to-welfare mechanism is not operationally closed on the deployed candidate occupation law with a controlled continuous-time bias.
The high-dimensional result certifies conservative improvement over a schedule but does not establish accurate solution of the HJB.
Final-simulation confidence is conditional on fixed trained policies and does not identify a method-level distribution over training randomness.
The work accounts do not yet produce a fully inclusive matched-accuracy comparison, and the cheaper raw method is at least as strong on the reported fixed-work evidence.
The comparator set does not isolate the contribution against direct neural HJB or other strong numerical alternatives.
The 63-page article and 144-page supplement retain a scope much broader than the model-specific verification contribution established by R14.
positive_findings: R14 is a complete source-bound publication snapshot rather than an unexecuted development branch.
Generic multilayer policies and critics are actually trained in dimensions 10, 20 and 50.
The direct method estimand is formed on common paths instead of subtracting separate lower bounds.
The capital certificate uses a model-specific payoff identity and diffusion-transfer account rather than a sampled residual shortcut.
The manuscript reports unfavorable critic diagnostics and unresolved direct method rankings without relabeling them as successes.
The evidence and preservation record is unusually strong and reproducible.

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun all time-budgeted training jobs; a new run would use a different hardware and timing environment and would not be an exact replay of the original wall-clock experiment.

The reviewer independently verified the source-bound delivery, deterministic aggregate tables, and one representative original raw fixed-work shard; the full 19-artifact identity ledger is taken from the source-bound publication audit.
No claim is made that an inconclusive policy-payoff interval proves equality or that the raw-costate method dominates NBO.
No inference about author intent is made from the mismatch between the paper's NBO framing and its method-agnostic verification result.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
